proof:
# A unique noncentral tetrahedral section coordinate need not have a large captured partner

Let Xi be uniform on the probability tetrahedron. Consider the actual strict quadrilateral section with raw margins

    c=(1/10,2,-1,-1).

Its positive side captures vertices 1 and 2. The section centroid is

    b=(56/165,47/225,559/2475,559/2475).             (1)

Consequently

    b_1-1/3=1/165>0,
    1/3-b_2=28/225>0,
    1/3-b_3=1/3-b_4=266/2475>0,
    b_3-b_2=b_4-b_2=14/825>0.                      (2)

Thus vertex 1 is the unique noncentral coordinate (meaning a section-centroid coordinate above 1/3), but its captured partner has the SMALLEST of the three remaining centroid coordinates. This refutes any classification shortcut asserting that a captured partner must be one of the two largest remaining coordinates.

Here is a direct exact verification. For raw margins (p,q,-r,-s), put X=1/p, Y=1/q, Z=1/r, W=1/s and L=X+Y+Z+W. Triangulation of the quadrilateral section gives

    3b_1=X/(X+Z)+X/(X+W)-X/L,
    3b_2=Y/(Y+Z)+Y/(Y+W)-Y/L,
    3b_3=Z/(Z+X)+Z/(Z+Y)-Z/L,
    3b_4=W/(W+X)+W/(W+Y)-W/L.

Substituting (X,Y,Z,W)=(10,1/2,1,1), L=25/2 yields (1). The coordinates sum to 1 and c dot b=0, as required for the actual section. All entries of c are nonzero, so there is no vertex-contact or improper-section exception.

This certificate concerns ONE actual section. It does not assert three common-centroid sections, positive balance, capacity maximality, or a violation of any OC depth bound. In particular it does not decide the conic chord sign between two actual sections sharing the same centroid. The two equal excluded centroid coordinates make this example especially simple; they do not validate an ordering shortcut in the unequal case.
